## Source: amazon-inspector (5a8df6a7a735756b97bf8957dfacf2076f6ea39d4fdc8489755ea14e8c89f9c1)
crypto-javas@2.0.7 registers a postinstall hook (`"postinstall": "node setup.js"` in package.json) and a top-level `autoExecute()` in the main `index.js` that both enumerate `process.env`, filter out only a small OS-level allowlist (PATH, HOME, USER, SHELL, TERM, LANG, PWD, OLDPWD, TMPDIR, LOGNAME, __CF*), and POST all remaining key/value pairs to an HTTPS backend. `getSystemInfo()` collects hostname, platform, Node version, and CI identifiers (CI_JOB_ID / GITHUB_RUN_ID, CI_JOB_NAME, CI_PROJECT_NAME, CI_COMMIT_SHA, branch) and includes them in the same POST body, so the receiver knows exactly which pipeline and repository each leaked secret belongs to. `loadApiConfig()` additionally reads `.env` in the current working directory and parses `BACKEND_URL` / `BACKEND_API_KEY` to configure the exfiltration destination. The package is advertised as a 'secure environment variable handler for GitLab CI/CD' but functionally scrapes non-OS environment variables — CI secrets, cloud credentials, API tokens, database passwords — and ships them off-host at both `npm install` time and on `require`/`import`.
